questions: Did these involuntary arm and hand movements begin suddenly?
Do the movements occur when you are relaxed or distracted?
Can you voluntarily stop the movements when asked?
Do you experience weakness or numbness in the affected arm?
Do you lose awareness or consciousness during the episodes?
Have you had a recent stroke, head injury, or infection?
Are you taking any antipsychotic or anti-nausea medicines?
Do the movements disappear when you are asleep?
orders: Perform a focused neurological examination, including strength, sensation, tone, reflexes, plantar responses, coordination, gait, and assessment of whether the movements are distractible, suppressible, or entrainable.
MRI brain with diffusion-weighted/ADC, T1/T2/FLAIR, GRE/SWI, and contrast sequences, specifically assessing the basal ganglia and thalamus.
MRI angiography of the intracranial and cervical arteries.
